# FundCalyx — full content (fundcalyx.com)

> FundCalyx is a subscription service that discovers U.S. federal grant
> opportunities, screens them against an organization's profile using the
> funder's full official notice, and monitors saved opportunities for
> deadline and notice changes. Operated by Apex Grid Engineering PLLC
> (Queen Creek, Arizona). Founded by Jeremy "Chico" Mills, Founder & CEO.

## Who it serves

Nonprofits, schools and education foundations, startups, and small
businesses that pursue U.S. federal grants and cannot afford to spend
weeks evaluating opportunities they were never eligible for.

## Coverage

Federal grant opportunities from Grants.gov only. Foundation, corporate
and most state grants are not included, and FundCalyx says so up front.

## How screening works

FundCalyx reads the funder's full official notice (not a listing summary)
and checks the organization's profile against each published eligibility
criterion. Every screening produces exactly one of three outcomes:

- Matches published criteria
- Does not match
- Cannot be determined

Every outcome is tied to the criterion and its supporting source passage.
If the notice cannot settle a question, the outcome is "cannot be
determined" — never a guess dressed up as a verdict. FundCalyx does not
decide or certify eligibility; the funder's determination governs.

## Monitoring

Monitoring runs daily, not in real time. Deadline reminders are sent at
30, 14, 7, and 2 days before a close date, and change alerts are sent
when a monitored notice changes. A blank close date in the source is
reported as "no deadline published" — never an invented date. If a data
feed cannot be verified, alerts pause and a visible stale-data notice is
shown rather than alerts being built on unverified data.

## What FundCalyx does not do

- Does not decide or certify eligibility.
- Does not write or submit applications (grant writing is not part of
  the subscription).
- Does not guarantee funding, and never charges a success fee.
- Never asks for, collects, or holds customers' Grants.gov or SAM.gov
  credentials.

## Plans

- Scout — $39/month: 1 organization profile, 1 seat, daily monitoring,
  weekly digest, deadline reminders and change alerts, basic CSV export.
- Match — $79/month: 3 profiles, 3 seats, daily monitoring, daily
  digest, monthly funding calendar, CSV export.
- Team — $149/month: 6 profiles, 5 seats, custom filtered digests,
  structured export, automated quarterly profile check.

Deadline monitoring is daily on every plan — deadline safety is never a
tier upgrade. FundCalyx sells assessed fit, not list access: there is no
free tier, and a dated sample report built from real federal records is
the pre-purchase evaluation mechanism.

## Sample report (real federal records, screened Nov 13, 2026)

The public sample report at https://fundcalyx.com/sample-report.html
shows one of each outcome, screened against the opportunities' published
detail pages:

1. MATCHES PUBLISHED CRITERIA — U.S. Department of Justice, Office of
   Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention (OJJDP), "FY 2026
   Mentoring for Youth Impacted by Opioids and Other Substance Use,"
   opportunity O-OJJDP-2026-172743. Closes November 16, 2026. Maximum
   award $2,000,000; total program funding $16,500,000; approximately 15
   awards. Screened profile: a 501(c)(3) statewide Arizona youth
   mentoring nonprofit.
2. DOES NOT MATCH — National Institutes of Health (NIH) SBIR parent
   announcement PA-27-100. Closes April 5, 2027. Amounts not specified
   in the source. Published criteria limit applicants to small business
   concerns, which disqualifies the nonprofit profile.
3. CANNOT BE DETERMINED — U.S. Department of Transportation / Federal
   Highway Administration, opportunity FHWA-GADC-27-001. Closes
   December 28, 2026. Maximum award $20,000,000. The open question is
   whether the profile organization may apply through a consortium path;
   the published material does not settle it.

Production screening runs against the full official notice; the sample
screens were run against the opportunities' published detail pages and
are labelled that way on the sample page itself.

## Frequently asked questions

Q: Is funding guaranteed?
A: No. A match is a starting point, not an eligibility determination or
an award guarantee. Always verify requirements and deadlines with the
original funder.

Q: Does FundCalyx write or submit applications?
A: No. FundCalyx focuses on opportunity discovery, eligibility
screening, source links, and deadline organization.

Q: Can I cancel a subscription?
A: Yes — self-service, anytime. Ordinary cancellation runs to the end
of the period you paid for. If FundCalyx ever ends your service itself,
the unused part of the period is refunded pro-rata.

Q: Where do the grants come from?
A: U.S. federal opportunities, via Grants.gov. Foundation, corporate
and most state grants are not in this data — FundCalyx is a
federal-grants tool and says so up front.

Q: How does screening actually work?
A: We read the funder's full official notice and check your profile
against each published eligibility criterion, keeping the source passage
behind every outcome. If the notice can't settle a question, the answer
is "cannot be determined" — never a guess dressed up as a verdict.

Q: How fast are change alerts?
A: Monitoring runs daily, not in real time. When a sweep detects a
change and verifies it, the alert is queued and sent — expect same-day
on a normal cycle, and we'll show a visible stale-data notice rather
than send alerts built on a feed we couldn't verify.

Q: What if FundCalyx gets a deadline wrong?
A: We notify you promptly, publish the correction, and assess the
impact. Where a correction can't restore what was lost — a passed
deadline can't be un-passed — the affected period is credited or
refunded under the refund policy. Corrections never erase the original
error from our accuracy record.

Q: Do you hold my Grants.gov or SAM.gov login?
A: Never. FundCalyx works from public funder data and the profile you
give us. Your portal credentials are yours alone, and we will never ask
for them.

## Refund policy (summary; the legal page governs)

If FundCalyx publishes a materially wrong deadline or screening outcome,
it notifies affected customers promptly, publishes a correction, and
assesses the impairment; where a correction cannot reasonably restore
the service, the affected period is credited or refunded. Full Terms,
Privacy, and Refund policy: https://fundcalyx.com/legal.html
